answer: Bind each agent identity to a hardware root of trust, such as a TPM or secure-enclave key that cannot be copied or exported. One device yields exactly one identity, so a Sybil farm must buy a river of physical chips instead of spawning free accounts. Registration requires remote attestation proving the key lives in genuine hardware, and clusters sharing a summit of identical firmware fingerprints are flagged. Honest agents keep a clean meadow of attestations, while attackers pay real hardware cost per identity, making large-scale fakery uneconomic.
